title: Recognizer Research
summary: First bounded rhythm execution is complete: four copied development recordings and six numerical controls. Historical per-record diagnosis is also complete. No improvement candidate or empirical musical gain is established.

milestones.title: Audit and research design
milestones.detail: Eight areas reviewed; native Dereck review obtained; 36-step protocol approved after two corrections. Protocol approval is not empirical validation.

milestones.title: Frozen rhythm baseline
milestones.detail: Ten rhythm-only executions completed: four copied local development recordings and six synthetic controls. Four adapter tests pass. Original source/audio checksums are retained; the full app was not run.

milestones.title: Task-separated scoring harness
milestones.detail: Independent BPM, pulse-level, beat/downbeat, literal-meter and availability channels; no universal scalar.

milestones.title: Blinded reference and source eligibility
milestones.detail: Two-annotator instructions and rights/overlap inventory. Existing guitar/drum diagnostic data remains development material.

milestones.title: Historical pulse-error diagnosis
milestones.detail: All 78 guitar and 115 drum retained predictions reaggregated. Nine missing-media exclusions remain explicit. Reference-informed correction is only an oracle diagnostic.

milestones.title: Independent validation of execution increment
milestones.detail: Review actual artifacts, source boundaries, scoring denominators and public-page security before promoting any result.

milestones.title: Independent musical confirmation
milestones.detail: No new blinded human labels or untouched-source confirmation study is available yet.

findings.title: Pulse-level mistakes dominate a large share of retained drum error
findings.detail: Using the predeclared descriptive 4% reference-relative half/double-nearness rule, 22 of 115 drum records account for 64.49% of summed exact relative error. The corresponding guitar values are 3 of 78 and 14.32%. This is retained-development arithmetic, not a new model gain or proof of perceptual correctness.
findings.confidence: HIGH for the retained arithmetic; generalization unestablished
findings.source: diagnosis/RESULTS.md and diagnosis.json, 2026-10-24; internal development evidence

findings.title: The frozen baseline reproduces a numerical half-rate case
findings.detail: On a synthetic 180-pulse-per-minute control, the unchanged estimator returns 89.1 BPM. Silence, DC and the tested sustained tone return unavailable BPM. These controls establish numerical behavior only, not musical accuracy.
findings.confidence: HIGH for this pinned execution only

blockers: Prediction-blinded musical annotation and untouched-source confirmation remain outstanding.
No improvement candidate is selected or promoted; no empirical paper is ready.
next_steps: Complete and independently check this bounded execution increment.
Use the reference inventory to choose rights-cleared, composition-grouped annotation sources.
Test one pulse-level mechanism only after a trustworthy diagnosis.

agents.responsibility: Blinded reference contract and source inventory

activity.title: Research execution authorized and dispatched
activity.action: Three disjoint native Codex agents; gpt-6.1-sol, model_reasoning_effort=medium.
activity.result: Running; no paid compute, source-app modification, audio/weight acquisition or submission.

activity.title: Frozen rhythm baseline and historical diagnosis completed
activity.action: Invocation summaries: run_baseline.py; unittest test_frozen_rhythm; reanalyse_rhythm.py and its self-tests. Existing local Python environments; no checkpoint/audio acquisition.
activity.result: Ten baseline/control cases finished; four adapter tests pass. Historical diagnosis reaggregates 193 inspected records. Independent execution/publication review still pending.

limits: Deployed checkpoints, not second-by-second monitoring. Refresh after a milestone deployment.
Synthetic controls test numerical behavior, not musical correctness.
Old diagnostic recordings are not fresh confirmation material.
CLPR remains the flagship. This is a proposed task-specific recognizer-qualification lane; rhythm/meter accuracy does not validate register or note-density constructs.
